Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the informant which is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned counsel for the informant learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in case crime No.345 of 2022,
under Sections 376, 452, 504, 506 IPC, police station Ramkola, District Kushinagar with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
4. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The allegations against applicant that on 10.03.2022 at 11.00 PM, applicant has forcibly trespassed into the house of prosecutrix and committed rape upon prosecutrix, are wholly false and inherently improbable.

Several other family Gulab Khatik vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22385785/
1 members were shown present in the house of prosecutrix and thus, the allegations levelled by prosecutrix do not inspire the confidence.

sentences.text: The prosecutrix is a mature and married lady.

It was submitted that in fact earlier an first information report was lodged by the applicant against the son of prosecutrix, which was registered on 28.09.2021, under Section 376, 147, 323, 504 and 506 IPC and in that matter bail application of son of prosecutrix was rejected by this Court on 06.07.2022 and after that the first information report of this case has been got lodged by moving an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.

Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that first information report of this case is a counter blast to the earlier case and it has been got lodged in order to pressurize the applicant for compromise in earlier case.

Learned counsel has referred the statement of prosecutrix, recorded under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., and submitted that the allegations that in the mid night applicant, in presence of other family members, committed rape upon prosecutrix, are wholly improbable.

Lastly, it has been submitted that the applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 08.01.2023, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
5. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for informant have opposed the bail application.

Learned counsel for informant submitted that earlier a case was lodged from the side of prosecutrix against applicant and others under Section 376, 452, 504 and 506 IPC on 13.07.2021 and after that applicant has got lodged an FIR against the son of prosecutrix by moving an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
It was submitted that prosecutrix has made allegations of rape against applicant.

6. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

7. Let the applicant-accused Gulab Khatik involved in aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
(i) The applicant-accused shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant-accused shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant-accused shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant-accused shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant-accused shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement,
threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade Gulab Khatik vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22385785/
2 them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
